title: Life Sprint

selected_top_5.reasoning: The entire loop models a compressed human lifespan with yearly choices around work, study, social life, health, money, and aging.
selected_top_5.uncertainty: Very low; this is the clearest mechanical identity.

selected_top_5.reasoning: Core play is about balancing health, happiness, money, and skill under constant attrition and tradeoffs.
selected_top_5.uncertainty: Low; the player is continuously allocating limited resources and absorbing random setbacks.

selected_top_5.reasoning: The player inhabits an abstract life role and shapes a career path and lifestyle through repeated personal choices rather than controlling movement in space.
selected_top_5.uncertainty: Moderate; it has roleplay flavor but remains highly system-driven.

selected_top_5.reasoning: The run unfolds as a sequence of short yearly updates, event log beats, promotions, and setbacks, creating a lightweight emergent life story.
selected_top_5.uncertainty: Moderate; there is no authored narrative tree, only systemic narrative progression.

selected_top_5.reasoning: The interface and pacing resemble a tap-driven stat game with quick repeatable inputs and immediate reward feedback.
selected_top_5.uncertainty: High; it is not idle or auto-generating, so this is more of a surface interaction resemblance than a true genre fit.

uncertainty_notes: The strongest overlap is between life simulation and resource management.

The game has some survival pressure, but not enough to rank 'Survival game' above the selected five because death is tied mainly to one stat and there is no crafting, exploration, or environmental threat loop.
It also has mild clicker and incremental qualities, but those are secondary to its life-choice structure.
